summary.title: Understanding Parser Combinators
summary.one_liner: You learn how parser combinators work by building a small F# parser library from scratch: a Parser wrapper type, pchar, andThen, orElse, and choice.
takeaways: A parser can be modelled as a wrapped function from input string to a Success or Failure result with remaining input.
Curried functions and partial application let a parser such as pchar 'A' be created once and reused.
Combinators andThen (.>>.), orElse (<|>) and choice build larger parsers out of smaller ones.
Error messages from simple combinators can be misleading; the author defers better error messages to a later post.
summary.summary: This is the first of a four-part series that builds a parser combinator library in F# incrementally, starting from a parser that matches a single hard-coded character. It moves through a char-matching function with error messages, a ParseResult choice type, currying and partial application, and a Parser wrapper type with a run helper. It then adds the andThen and orElse combinators, a choice function over lists, and anyOf. The post is explicit that performance is not the focus and points readers to FParsec for real use.
